retrieval_method: parallel-cli extract on the NEJM full text (two independent passes: whole article, then a second pass anchored on #methods for the randomisation conditions). Direct curl of nejm.org returns HTTP 403. Cross-checked against the Cochrane review 'Characteristics of included studies' entry for Chen 2016 and against Cochrane Analysis 3.1, both read from a PDF I rendered myself from Europe PMC (https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC8095009?pdf=render).
quote_found: Frozen-embryo transfer resulted in a higher frequency of live birth after the first transfer than did fresh-embryo transfer (49.3% vs. 42.0%), for a rate ratio of 1.17 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05 to 1.31; P=0.004).
verification_notes: Every component checked against the source, not the claim. POPULATION: 'A total of 1508 infertile women with the polycystic ovary syndrome who were undergoing their first IVF cycle...All the women were between the ages of 20 and 34 years and weighed at least 40 kg' and 'we used modified Rotterdam criteria...which included menstrual abnormalities (irregular uterine bleeding, oligomenorrhea, or amenorrhea) combined with either hyperandrogenism or polycystic ovaries'. The claim's randomisation condition is also verbatim correct: 'On the day of oocyte retrieval, if an adequate number of oocytes (>3 and <30) were retrieved and the patient was at low risk for the ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (as determined by local investigators), patients were randomly assigned to one of the two study groups in a 1:1 ratio, stratified according to study site.' EMBRYOS: DET confirmed twice - 'women underwent the transfer of up to two fresh or frozen embryos' and 'On day 4 of the progesterone regimen, two day-3 frozen embryos were thawed and transferred.' TIMING: per-transfer confirmed - 'The primary outcome was a live birth, which was defined as delivery of any viable infant at 28 weeks or more of gestation during the first embryo transfer.' TRIGGER: 'Urinary human chorionic gonadotropin at a dose of 4000 to 8000 IU' with 'Gonadotropin-releasing-hormone antagonist (Cetrorelix, Merck Serono) at a daily dose of 250 ug'. ENDOMETRIAL PREP: 'Oral estradiol valerate (Progynova, Delpharm Lille) was administered for endometrial preparation on day 2 or 3 of the second menstrual cycle after oocyte retrieval. Intramuscular progesterone at a dose of 80 mg per day was added when the endometrial thickness reached 8 mm or more'. ARM DENOMINATORS independently corroborated: Cochrane Analysis 3.1 lists Chen 2016 as 368/746 versus 320/762 for live birth after the first transfer, i.e. 49.33% versus 42.0%, exactly reproducing the trial's reported percentages and the 746/762 denominators.

retrieval_method: Two independent sources. (a) Trial statement: parallel-cli extract of https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1513873. (b) Cumulative arm counts: I downloaded the Cochrane review PDF MYSELF from Europe PMC (PMC8095009, 87-page Apache FOP PDF, md5 2c45efe16b57dd87f1eb727b1a0ae157), ran pdftotext -layout, then rendered PDF page 23 (journal page 20) with pdftoppm at 160 dpi and READ THE IMAGE DIRECTLY. This is a different file from the Amsterdam UMC repository copy the first agent used (that one is an 88-page OpenPDF re-wrap; different md5).
quote_found: There was no significant between-group difference in the cumulative live-birth rate, including all frozen-embryo transfers performed within 12 months after the initial transfer (P=0.30) (Table S9 in the Supplementary Appendix).
verification_notes: FIGURE READ VISUALLY BY ME. Cochrane Figure 4 ('Forest plot of comparison 1. Freeze-all versus conventional IVF, outcomes per woman, outcome 1.1 live birth rate'). The Chen 2016 row reads Events 465, Total 746 (freeze-all) versus Events 455, Total 762 (conventional IVF), Weight 34.1%, Odds Ratio M-H Fixed 1.12 [0.91 , 1.37]. It sits under the subgroup header '1.1.1 Live birth rate: cumulatively for cleavage stage transfer', whose Subtotal diamond is 1.09 [0.93 , 1.29] and crosses the null. THE SUBGROUP HEADERS ON THIS PLOT ARE BY EMBRYO STAGE, NOT BY POPULATION. Vuong 2018 (the explicitly non-PCOS trial, 191/391 vs 185/391, OR 1.06 [0.80, 1.41]) sits in the SAME cleavage-stage subgroup as Chen 2016 (the PCOS trial), directly adjacent to it. Timing label 'cumulative' is correct and is the axis on which the claim turns.

retrieval_method: parallel-cli extract on the NEJM full text (Table 3 returned in full as a markdown table). Population/eligibility independently cross-checked against the Cochrane review 'Characteristics of included studies: Shi 2018' entry, read from the Europe PMC PDF I rendered myself. Arm counts independently cross-checked against Cochrane Analysis 3.1.
quote_found: There was no significant difference in the rate of live birth between the frozen-embryo group and the fresh-embryo group (48.7% and 50.2%, respectively; relative risk, 0.97; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.89 to 1.06; P=0.50) (Table 3).
verification_notes: NUMBERS: Table 3 row 'Primary outcome: live birth - no. (%)' reads 525 (48.7) | 542 (50.2) | -1.5 (-5.7 to 2.8) | 0.97 (0.89 to 1.06) | 0.50, with column headers 'Frozen-Embryo Group (N=1077)' and 'Fresh-Embryo Group (N=1080)'. Every figure in the claim matches exactly, including that the absolute difference and its CI are REPORTED, not computed. Cochrane Analysis 3.1 independently lists Shi 2018 as 525/1077 versus 542/1080. POPULATION IS GENUINELY OVULATORY, NOT JUST ADJECTIVALLY SO: NEJM Methods, Trial Population - 'Eligible women were 20 to 35 years of age, had a normal menstrual cycle (defined as a spontaneous cycle length of >=21 days and <=35 days), and a duration of infertility of more than 1 year.' The Cochrane characteristics table states the exclusion explicitly: 'women with a history of unilateral oophorectomy, recurrent spontaneous abortion, diagnosis of the PCOS, or uterine abnormality...were excluded.' So PCOS really was an exclusion criterion. EMBRYOS: 'Up to two cleavage-stage embryos were transferred in each participant' (Abstract Methods), and Cochrane: 'On day 2 or 3 of the embryo culture, up to 2 embryos were selected and transferred.' TIMING: 'The primary outcome was live birth after the first transfer (fresh- or frozen-embryo transfer).' ONE ANNOTATION IN THE CLAIM OBJECT IS SUPERSEDED (does not affect the claim itself): the field freezing_method says 'not stated in the retrieved full text - I could NOT verify vitrification versus slow freezing for this trial'. The NEJM full text DOES state it: 'In women who were assigned to the frozen-embryo group, all the embryos were vitrified. Two good-quality embryos were vitrified on day 2 or day 3...'. Cochrane concurs: 'day 2 or 3 embryo cryopreservation by means of vitrification'. This is a retrieval-limitation hedge, not a factual error about the trial, and the number, population and timing all match, so the claim stands.

retrieval_method: parallel-cli extract on the NEJM full text; the Discussion was returned and I located the passage verbatim rather than searching for the claimed string.
quote_found: Our previous trial involving women with the polycystic ovary syndrome, which used a protocol that was nearly identical to that used in the present trial, showed a favorable effect of frozen-embryo transfer on the rate of live birth. The reason for the discrepant results in these two trial populations is uncertain.
verification_notes: Quoted verbatim, including the sentence order. In the source a footnote marker sits between the two sentences ('...on the rate of live birth. [6] The reason for the discrepant results...'); the claim drops the marker, which is standard and non-distorting. The next sentence in the source is 'We speculate that the difference is due to the unfavorable uterine environment after fresh-embryo transfer in women with the polycystic ovary syndrome, as shown by a much lower rate of live birth overall in the previous trial than in the present trial.' - i.e. the authors offer a SPECULATION, which reinforces rather than undermines the claim that no formal test was done. I searched the full retrieved Discussion for any interaction p-value, pooled model or formal cross-trial comparison and found none.

retrieval_method: parallel-cli extract on the NEJM full text, three passes (whole article; Discussion + Study Population; Discussion + IVF Treatment). Eligibility independently cross-checked against the Cochrane 'Characteristics of included studies: Vuong 2018' entry; arm counts independently cross-checked against Cochrane Analysis 3.1.
quote_found: Live births occurred in 132 women (33.8%) in the frozen-embryo group and in 123 women (31.5%) in the fresh-embryo group, for a between-group difference of 2.3 percentage points (95% CI, -4.5 to 9.1; risk ratio, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.88 to 1.31; P=0.54).
verification_notes: PRIMARY OUTCOME (ongoing pregnancy, per-transfer): 'Ongoing pregnancy after the first completed cycle occurred in 142 of 391 women (36.3%) in the frozen-embryo group and in 135 of 391 (34.5%) in the fresh-embryo group, for a between-group difference of 1.8 percentage points (95% confidence interval [CI], -5.2 to 8.7; risk ratio, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.87 to 1.27; P=0.65)'. Table 2 confirms both the ongoing-pregnancy and live-birth rows. NON-PCOS POPULATION VERIFIED FROM ELIGIBILITY, NOT THE TITLE: 'They were excluded if they had a history of the polycystic ovary syndrome (on the basis of the Rotterdam criteria), were undergoing in vitro maturation with polycystic ovaries visible on ultrasonography, or had undergone oocyte donation' and 'had undergone no more than one previous IVF cycle'. The claim's careful distinction that the population is non-PCOS rather than strictly ovulatory is CORRECT and I verified the baseline row myself: 'Ovulation disorder other than PCOS | 22 (5.6) | 33 (8.4)'. EMBRYOS: 'A maximum of two embryos of grade 1 or 2 were thawed on the day of embryo transfer, 3 days after the start of progesterone' and 'Our study included the transfer of two embryos and universal intracytoplasmic sperm injection.' TRIGGER FIELD FULLY VERIFIED, INCLUDING THE >15 FOLLICLE DETAIL: 'Women at high risk for the ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome were not included in our trial, owing to our practice of routinely administering gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist to trigger oocyte maturation in women with more than 15 follicles on the day of hCG administration to minimize the risk of ovarian hyperstimulation; the use of gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist was an exclusion criterion for our trial.' ENDOMETRIAL PREP verified verbatim: 'oral estradiol valerate (Valiera...) at a dose of 8 mg per day, starting on the second or third day of the menstrual cycle...vaginal progesterone (Cyclogest, Actavis) at a dose of 800 mg per day was started when the endometrial thickness reached 8 mm or more'. Cryotech vitrification verified. The claim's cumulative note is also verbatim correct: 'The cumulative 12-month rate of live birth in women who had completed 12 months of follow-up was 48.8% in the frozen-embryo group and 47.3% in the fresh-embryo group (risk ratio, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.89 to 1.19; P=0.72).'

retrieval_method: parallel-cli extract on the NEJM full text; I regex-searched the returned Discussion text for the substrings 'not necessarily inconsistent' and 'overlap' and recovered the sentence in two separate extraction passes.
quote_found: However, our findings are not necessarily inconsistent with those reported in women with the polycystic ovary syndrome, because the 95% confidence intervals around the risk ratios for live birth that were associated with frozen-embryo transfer in our trial overlap with the 95% confidence intervals in that report.
verification_notes: Verbatim match (the source has a footnote marker '27' immediately before 'However'). I checked the arithmetic behind the authors' assertion independently: Vuong's live-birth RR is 1.07 (0.88 to 1.31) and Chen's is 1.17 (1.05 to 1.31), so Vuong's interval does contain Chen's point estimate and the two intervals overlap over 1.05-1.31. The claim's characterisation - an author-stated acknowledgement that the PCOS/non-PCOS difference is not statistically established, made by eyeballing intervals rather than by any test - is accurate. No interaction test, pooled model or meta-regression appears anywhere in the retrieved Discussion.

retrieval_method: parallel-cli extract on the Lancet URL returned the structured Summary only (Background/Methods/Findings/Interpretation) plus the reference list - the Methods section itself is NOT exposed, exactly as the claim states. I therefore verified the design claims from two further sources I retrieved independently: (a) the Cochrane 'Characteristics of included studies: Wei 2019' entry from the Europe PMC PDF (PMC8095009) I rendered myself; (b) the trial's own published protocol, Wei D et al., Trials 2017;18:253, retrieved as JATS XML from Europe PMC at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC5460334/fullTextXML.
quote_found: Frozen single blastocyst transfer resulted in higher rates of singleton livebirth than did fresh single blastocyst transfer (416 [50%] vs 329 [40%]; relative risk [RR] 1.26, 95% CI 1.14-1.41, p<0.0001).
verification_notes: NUMBERS: verbatim from the Lancet Findings. Denominators verified from the same Summary: '825 women were assigned to each group and included in analyses.' 416/825 = 50.4%, 329/825 = 39.9%, so the ~10.5 percentage point figure the claim computes is right. POPULATION: '1650 women with regular menstrual cycles undergoing their first cycle of in-vitro fertilisation were enrolled from Aug 1, 2016, to June 3, 2017' and Interpretation 'in ovulatory women with good prognosis'. The protocol's eligibility criteria are verbatim as claimed: 'Women aged >=20 and <35 years; Women with regular menses (defined as a spontaneous cycle length of 21-35 days); Women who are undergoing their first cycle of IVF or intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI); Women with >=4 day-3 embryos suitable for transfer.' Cochrane's independent extraction of the eligibility criteria agrees. NOTE I CHECKED SPECIFICALLY: PCOS is NOT listed as an explicit exclusion criterion in Wei 2019, but the regular-menses inclusion criterion (21-35 day cycles) excludes oligo/anovulatory PCOS, so the 'ovulatory' label is earned by the eligibility criteria and not merely by the title. EMBRYOS - SET CONFIRMED THREE WAYS: Lancet Summary 'a delayed frozen-thawed single blastocyst transfer was done'; Cochrane 'For the fresh blastocyst transfer group, a single blastocyst was selected and transferred on day 5 of embryo culture'; protocol 'a single fresh blastocyst transfer group and a single frozen blastocyst transfer group (all blastocysts vitrified and a deferred frozen blastocyst transfer)'. TRIGGER from protocol, verbatim as claimed: 'GnRH antagonist ganirelix...at a daily dose of 250 ug...Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) at a dose of 4000-10,000 IU will be administered when at least two follicles are >=18 mm in mean diameter.' ENDOMETRIAL PREP from protocol, verbatim as claimed: 'At least 4 weeks later, endometrium preparation is performed with a natural cycle regimen or hormone replacement cycle regimen, at the discretion of local investigators...Local investigators decide whether to use hCG for ovulation triggering according to their clinical routine.' OUTCOME LABELLING IS CORRECT AND IMPORTANT: the trial primary outcome is SINGLETON livebirth (416 vs 329). Cochrane Analysis 3.1 extracts overall live birth after the first transfer for the same trial as 439/825 versus 341/825, OR 1.61 [1.33, 1.96] - a different, larger pair of numbers. The claim correctly labels its figures as singleton live birth, so there is no conflict, but any downstream text must not swap them.

retrieval_method: I downloaded the Cochrane review PDF myself from Europe PMC (PMC8095009), extracted text with pdftotext -layout, and rendered page 23 (journal page 20) to PNG with pdftoppm at 160 dpi and read the image directly. Confirmed in both the Figure 4 rendering and the separate Analysis 1.1 data table later in the same PDF.
verification_notes: FIGURE READ VISUALLY BY ME. The Wei 2019 row reads 627/825 freeze-all versus 604/825 conventional IVF, weight 29.1%, OR 1.16 [0.93 , 1.45], with the point estimate right of the null but the interval crossing 1. It sits under '1.1.2 Live birth rate: cumulatively for blastocyst stage transfer', whose Subtotal is 1.06 [0.88 , 1.27]. SUBGROUP HEADERS ARE BY EMBRYO STAGE, NOT BY POPULATION - I enumerated every subgroup header in the whole review (see SQ3-C10) and there is no ovulatory/PCOS axis anywhere. Timing label 'cumulative' is correct: this is outcome 1.1 'Cumulative live birth rate', which is per woman randomised, and it is the counterpart to the trial's per-transfer singleton result in SQ3-C7. The claim's arithmetic (627/825 = 76.0%, 604/825 = 73.2%) is right and is correctly flagged as computed rather than reported.

retrieval_method: Europe PMC REST fullTextXML for PMC7399608 (the BMJ open-access version of record), 121 KB of JATS XML which I stripped to text and searched directly. Design details independently cross-checked against the Cochrane 'Characteristics of included studies: Stormlund 2020' entry from the PDF I rendered myself, and arm counts against Cochrane Analysis 3.1.
quote_found: In the freeze-all group, 62 of 223 women (27.8%) had an ongoing pregnancy compared with 68 of 230 (29.6%) in the fresh transfer group, with a difference between groups of -1.8 (95% confidence interval -10.5 to 7.0; risk ratio 0.98, 95% confidence interval 0.87 to 1.10, P=0.76; table 3).
verification_notes: Verbatim match including the absolute difference and its CI, which are indeed reported rather than computed. TIMING: 'per-woman-randomised' is right - the primary outcome is 'the ongoing pregnancy rate defined as a detectable fetal heart beat after eight weeks of gestation' analysed by intention to treat, and Cochrane records it as 'ongoing pregnancy rate per randomised participant, which also included natural conceptions'. Consistently, 'Five women (2.3%) in the freeze-all group conceived naturally during the pause between oocyte retrieval and blastocyst transfer.' SET CLAIM VERIFIED WITH ITS EXCEPTIONS, VERBATIM: 'all randomised women had single blastocyst transfer apart from three women randomised to the fresh transfer group, of which two (0.9%) had single cleavage stage transfer and one (0.4%) had double cleavage stage transfer.' DIFFERENTIAL TRIGGER VERIFIED, VERBATIM: 'Final oocyte maturation was induced by administering 0.5 mg of a gonadotropin releasing hormone agonist (buserelin: Suprefact, Sanofi) in the freeze-all strategy group or 250 ug of human chorionic gonadotropin (choriongonadotropin alpha: Ovitrelle, Merck) in the fresh transfer strategy group. Women randomised to the fresh transfer strategy group received gonadotropin releasing hormone agonist triggering if more than 18 follicles with a mean diameter larger than 11 mm were present on the day of ovulation triggering...' POPULATION: the article title is 'Freeze-all versus fresh blastocyst transfer strategy during in vitro fertilisation in women with regular menstrual cycles'; Cochrane's eligibility extraction confirms 'Women with regular menses (defined as a spontaneous cycle length of >= 24 days and <= 35 days)', 'Aged 18-39 years', 'first, second or third cycle', 'normal or high responds (defined by serum AMH levels > 6.28 pmol/L...)', and that PCOS is NOT among the listed exclusions - exactly the nuance the claim states. Live-birth note verified: '61 of 223 (27.4%) and 66 of 230 (28.7%), respectively; risk ratio 0.98, 95% confidence interval 0.87 to 1.10, P=0.83', and Cochrane Analysis 3.1 independently lists Stormlund 2020 as 61/223 versus 66/230. Cochrane also confirms cumulative data were deferred: 'cumulative data will be accounted for in separate publications', so this trial contributes no cumulative estimate.

retrieval_method: Europe PMC PDF render of PMC8095009 downloaded by me (87 pages), pdftotext -layout for the text and pdftoppm page 23 rendered to PNG and read as an image. Note: the Europe PMC fullTextXML endpoint returns HTTP 404 for this record and cochranelibrary.com returns a Cloudflare 403 to curl, so the Europe PMC PDF render was the working route. I then EXHAUSTIVELY ENUMERATED every subgroup header and every analysis title in the whole review with regex rather than trusting the figure alone.
quote_found: We had planned to perform subanalyses on timing of cryopreservation (e.g. day of embryo development) and method of cryopreservation (e.g. slow freezing or vitrification). However, data were insufficient to conduct all planned subgroup analyses.
verification_notes: THE NEGATIVE IS EXHAUSTIVELY VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. I extracted every subgroup header of the form n.n.n across the entire 87-page review. The complete set is: 1.1.1/1.1.2 cleavage vs blastocyst stage; 1.2.1 per cycle with ovarian hyperstimulation; 1.3.1/1.3.2 cleavage vs blastocyst; 1.4.1/1.4.2 cleavage vs blastocyst; 1.5.1/1.5.2, 1.6.1/1.6.2, 1.7.1/1.7.2, 1.8.1/1.8.2, 1.9.1/1.9.2, 1.10.1/1.10.2, 1.11.1/1.11.2, 1.12.1/1.12.2, 1.13.1/1.13.2, 1.14.1/1.14.2 all cumulatively vs after first embryo transfer; 1.16.1/1.16.2 singletons vs multiples. There is NO PCOS, anovulatory, ovulatory or population subgroup anywhere in the review. The three comparisons are: 1 outcomes per woman, 2 adverse events per clinical pregnancy, 3 additional analysis live birth rate after first transfer. FORMAL TEST ON THE PRIMARY OUTCOME, verbatim from my own reading of both the figure image and the Analysis 1.1 table: 'Test for subgroup differences: Chi2 = 0.07, df = 1 (P = 0.78), I2 = 0%' - and the two subgroups it compares are cleavage stage versus blastocyst stage. POOLED NUMBERS verified: Total (95% CI) 2342 versus 2370, Total events 1463 versus 1440, OR 1.08 [0.95 , 1.22], 8 RCTs. POPULATION DESCRIPTION verified verbatim: 'studies had distinct inclusion criteria leading to the inclusion of select groups of women (women with a high risk of OHSS, good prognosis women, women with polycystic ovary syndrome, young women without polycystic ovary syndrome and in women with any IVF indication, including the women with possible low ovarian response)'. The claim's notes are also verbatim correct: 'This should be taken into account when considering the freeze all strategy, whether to use it in an unselected population or only in women with a good prognosis, with a minimum number of good-quality embryos available. The current review does not provide an answer to this.' And the additional analysis: 'Based on this calculation the live birth rate after the first transfer is increased following the freeze all strategy (OR 1.17, 95% CI 1.06 to 1.28; 13 RCTs, 7766 women) for all stages of transfer.' I read Analysis 3.1 in full and its bottom line reads 'Test for subgroup differences: Not applicable', i.e. even the first-transfer analysis has no subgrouping at all.

retrieval_method: WebFetch on the OUP article page, THREE independent passes with different prompts and different URL query strings to defeat caching. This was the only route that worked: parallel-cli extract returned network_error on the article page and fetch_error on the article-pdf URL; curl with browser headers returned HTTP 403 from Cloudflare on both the PDF and the doi.org redirect; headless Chromium via Playwright also received HTTP 403; the Wayback Machine snapshot of the PDF turned out to be a captured Cloudflare challenge page, not the PDF.
quote_found: To evaluate the effect of ovarian response on pregnancy outcomes after frozen and fresh embryo transfer, two series of multivariable logistic regression models were built in women with PCOS and in ovulatory women, respectively, with backward process for variable selection.
verification_notes: I TRIED HARD TO REFUTE THIS AND COULD NOT. The Statistical analysis subsection, read verbatim, specifies exactly two model series, both fitted WITHIN a cohort: 'The first serial models included age, body mass index (BMI), duration of infertility, previous pregnancy, oocyte number (as a continuous variable), randomization groups (frozen vs fresh embryo transfer), and interaction between randomization groups and oocyte number. The second serial models included age, BMI, duration of infertility, previous pregnancy, peak estradiol level (estradiol level on the day of hCG administration, as a continuous variable), randomization groups, and interaction between randomization groups and estradiol level. A significant interaction was defined as P value <= 0.05.' Both interaction terms are treatment-by-OVARIAN-RESPONSE. Neither is treatment-by-PCOS-status. RESULTS verbatim: 'In women with PCOS, after adjustment for age, BMI, duration of infertility, and previous pregnancy, the interaction between oocyte number and randomization groups (frozen vs fresh embryo transfer) was statistically significant for the rates of clinical pregnancy loss and live birth (P < 0.001)'; 'There was also a significant interaction between peak estradiol level and randomization groups for the rates of clinical pregnancy loss and live birth (P < 0.001)'; 'In ovulatory women, neither the interaction between oocyte number and randomization groups nor the interaction between peak estradiol level and randomization groups was statistically significant for any pregnancy outcome.' On three separate fetches I asked directly whether any pooled model across both cohorts with a group-by-PCOS-status interaction exists; the answer was no each time, and the supporting text is always the 'respectively' sentence above. TABLE 2 VERIFIED CELL BY CELL: PCOS >=16 oocytes 160/295 (54.8%) frozen versus 123/292 (42.1%) fresh, OR 1.67 (1.20-2.31); ovulatory >=16 oocytes 136/263 (51.7%) versus 128/251 (51.0%), OR 1.03 (0.73-1.45). Both match the claim exactly. Also verified: 'In the trial of ovulatory women, 74.2% of patients had FET after natural ovulatory cycle and 25.8% patients had FET after a programmed cycle' and 'Two cleavage-stage embryos were thawed and transferred.' The paper's own framing sentence is a claim rather than a test, as the claim object says: 'In this post hoc subgroup analysis of two large randomized trials, we found that the relative effect of FET vs fresh embryo transfer on pregnancy outcomes varied between women with PCOS and ovulatory women independently of ovarian response.' The claim's residual caveat about Supplemental Tables 1-5 is honest: I confirmed those five supplements are referenced but I could not open them, so I cannot exclude a pooled term hidden there. Nothing in the Methods, Results or Discussion reports one. SEPARATE ADVERSARIAL CHECK ON THE 'ONLY SOURCE' SUPERLATIVE: I found one other study using data from both the PCOS and the ovulatory trials - Yu Y et al., Reprod Biomed Online 2020;41:395-401 (PMID 32600942), a secondary analysis of all three trials (1508 PCOS, 2157 ovulatory cleavage, 1650 ovulatory blastocyst). Its stratifier is progesterone concentration on the hCG day, not PCOS status, and its conclusion is framed by ovarian response ('In women with normal or high ovarian response...'). I could not open its Methods (rbmojournal.com and sciencedirect.com both returned 403 to WebFetch; parallel-cli returned only the abstract and reference list), so I cannot state whether it fits any trial-by-treatment interaction term. It does not report an interaction by PCOS status in anything I could read. This does not overturn the operative assertion, which is about what Wei 2018 JCEM did and did not report.

retrieval_method: NCBI E-utilities efetch XML for the structured abstract of PMID 30689865 (the numbers), plus WebFetch on https://academic.oup.com/humrep/article/34/3/491/5306150 for the full text (parallel-cli extract returned network_error on that URL). The refutation came from NCBI efetch XML for PMID 30388233 (Roque 2019) and from the Cochrane review PDF I rendered myself.
quote_found: In high responders, a significantly higher probability of live birth was observed in the frozen ET group when compared with the fresh ET group (RR: 1.18, 95% CI: 1.06-1.31; fixed effects model; heterogeneity: I2 = 0%; three studies; n = 3398 patients). However the probability of live birth was not significantly different between the frozen ET group and the fresh ET group in normal responders (RR: 1.13, 95% CI: 0.90-1.41; random effects model; heterogeneity: I2 = 77%; three studies; n = 1608 patients).
what_is_wrong: The claim opens with a false uniqueness assertion: 'The ONLY meta-analysis that stratifies freeze-all versus fresh transfer by a physiological proxy for the PCOS/ovulatory axis (Bosdou 2019, by ovarian responder type)'. It is not the only one, and the other one predates it. Roque M, Haahr T, Geber S, Esteves SC, Humaidan P. 'Fresh versus elective frozen embryo transfer in IVF/ICSI cycles: a systematic review and meta-analysis of reproductive outcomes.' Hum Reprod Update 2019;25(1):2-14, PMID 30388233, doi 10.1093/humupd/dmy033, stratifies on exactly the same axis. Its abstract states verbatim: 'Subgroup analyses included normal and hyper-responder patients, embryo developmental stage on the day of embryo transfer, freezing method and the route of progesterone administration for luteal phase support in eFET cycles' and 'Subgroup analyses indicated higher LBRs by eFET than by fresh embryo transfer in hyper-responders (RR = 1.16; 95% CI: 1.05-1.28) and in PGT-A cycles (RR = 1.55; 95% CI: 1.14-2.10). However, no differences were observed for LBR in normo-responders (RR = 1.03; 95% CI: 0.91-1.17)'. On WebFetch of the Roque full text the strata are labelled explicitly as 'PCOS/hyper-responder patients' versus 'non-PCOS/normo-responders' with 4 studies/2035 patients and 3 studies/3076 patients respectively - i.e. Roque stratifies on the PCOS/ovulatory axis MORE directly than Bosdou does, not merely by proxy. The Cochrane review names both in the same breath, verbatim: 'Two recently published systematic reviews and meta-analyses, Roque 2019 and Bosdou 2019 reported a higher live birth rate after the first transfer in the freeze all strategy compared to conventional IVF/ICSI... In Roque 2019 this increased live birth rate was only found in hyper-responders and in cycles with PGT-A.' This omission is material rather than pedantic, because the claim's substantive argument is that the apparent subgroup difference is 'a difference in precision, not in effect size'. That argument is weaker once Roque is included: Roque's strata differ by 0.13 on the RR scale (1.16 versus 1.03), nearly three times Bosdou's 0.05 gap, and Roque's normo-responder interval (0.91-1.17) is tight rather than wide, so the null result there cannot be dismissed as imprecision. Everything else in the claim checks out: both relative risks and both confidence intervals are verbatim correct, the population description is correct, the timing (live birth after the FIRST frozen transfer in a freeze-only strategy) is correct, and the limitation sentence is verbatim correct - 'the analysis did not apply a standard for determining high or normal responders since the type of ovarian response followed the characterisation of populations as reported by the authors of the eligible studies'. I also independently confirm the claim's two flagged caveats: (i) WebFetch of the Bosdou full text reports that no formal test for subgroup differences, interaction test or meta-regression is present, so 'no interaction test is reported' stands; (ii) the published abstract really is internally inconsistent on stratum sizes - it states four RCTs with n=3255 in normal responders and four RCTs with n=2010 in high responders, yet the live-birth analysis reports n=3398 in high responders, which exceeds the stated high-responder total. The fix is to delete the word 'only' and add Roque 2019 as a second, concordant, earlier subgroup meta-analysis.

retrieval_method: NCBI E-utilities efetch XML for PMID 33006114, parsed directly. Europe PMC records this article as subscription-only with no PMCID, so the abstract is the ceiling for open retrieval; I did not pursue the paywalled full text because the claim is scoped to the abstract.
quote_found: There is no significant difference between frozen embryo transfer (FET) and fresh embryo transfer in ovulatory women or women with non-PCOS. We recommend that the transfer depends on the actual situation in the patient in clinical practice, rather than the "freeze all" policy and thawing FET.
verification_notes: Quote is verbatim, including the internal double quotes around 'freeze all'. Every element of the claim sentence is supported by the abstract I read: FOUR RCTs - 'In 511 identified studies, 4 were eligible and were included in this review'; OUTCOMES - 'There was no difference in live birth rate, singleton birth weight, clinical pregnancy, ongoing pregnancy, gestational diabetes, and gestational hypertension between frozen and fresh embryos. In frozen embryos, the relative risk of moderate or severe ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) was lower, the incidence rate of pre-eclampsia higher, and the standardized mean difference of twin birth weight higher than in fresh embryos.' POPULATION - the title is 'Pregnancy Outcome Difference between Fresh and Frozen Embryos in Women without Polycystic Ovary Syndrome' and the purpose statement reads 'to identify that the advantages of frozen embryos are not evident in ovulatory women or women with non-polycystic ovary syndrome (non-PCOS)'. The abstract does not name the four constituent RCTs, so the claim's honest flag that overlap with Wei 2019 is unverified is correct and I could not resolve it either. The claim's own instruction to weight this source below the primary trials is appropriate.

retrieval_method: Europe PMC REST fullTextXML for PMC9297209 (the BMJ Open open-access protocol) plus NCBI E-utilities efetch XML for PMID 35851030. For the negative half of the claim I ran an independent multi-route search for a results publication: six targeted PubMed E-utilities queries, two parallel-cli web searches, and a hand check of every candidate hit.
quote_found: We will invite the lead investigators of eligible trials to join the Individual participant data meta-analysis of trials comparing frozen versus fresh embryo transfer strategy (INFORM) collaboration and share the deidentified individual participant data (IPD) of their trials. We will harmonise the IPD and perform a two-stage meta-analysis and examine treatment-covariate interactions for important baseline characteristics.
verification_notes: Quote is verbatim from the Methods and analysis section of the abstract. The claim's other quoted fragments are verbatim too: 'The primary outcome will be live birth resulting from the first embryo transfer', 'PROSPERO registration number: CRD42021296566', and 'it is unclear which couples would benefit most from each policy, how and under which protocols'. THE NEGATIVE HALF IS INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED, WITH THE SEARCH RUN FRESH IN JULY 2026, four years after the protocol. A PubMed search for the registration number CRD42021296566 returns exactly one record: the protocol itself. A PubMed search for freeze-all AND 'individual participant data' AND meta-analysis returns exactly two records: the protocol, and PMID 41966094, which I retrieved and confirmed is an unrelated 2026 Human Reproduction meta-analysis of PGT-A obstetric and neonatal outcomes by Hyttel et al. A PubMed search for (freeze-all OR 'freeze all') AND ('treatment-covariate' OR 'treatment covariate') returns only the protocol. Two parallel-cli web searches aimed explicitly at an INFORM results publication returned only the protocol and its institutional repository mirrors (PMC, Monash, Aberdeen AURA, Oxford ORA, ResearchGate). NO RESULTS PAPER EXISTS AS OF THIS SEARCH. The claim's framing - that the definitive interaction analysis is registered and pending, not published - is correct and is itself the honest answer to SQ3.
